title: On The Front Lines: Taylor Bayless supports Southern California wildfire survivors as USACE safety specialist
description:
Taylor Bayless, U.S. Army Corps of Engineers safety specialist and St. Louis District employee, is supporting the Southern California wildfire recovery efforts in Altadena, California. 

She describes the purpose and responsibilities of her position as she works to support the wildfires survivors while ensure that the crews removing debris do it safely and in accordance with policies and laws
.
USACE currently has more than 450 personnel on site and around 3,000 contractors actively supporting our local, state and FEMA partners to support survivors impacted by the Palisades and Eaton fires Jan. 7. This includes engineers, debris removal crews, safety officers, quality assurance specialists and more from across the nation....

transcript.text: I'm out here in Altadena , serving on a
team of subject matter experts . My
particular role is as a safety
specialist . I try to view all of the
problems and the issues that come up
through a safety lens . A typical day
for me includes briefing the QAs on any
lessons learned , working with the
contractors' safety to resolve any
problems that arise , and responding to
any near misses or mishaps that happen
out in the field throughout the day .
On a debris mission such as this , it
presents a lot of unique safety hazards
that we have to account for . There's a
lot of moving parts that create
Instances of mishaps or near misses .
So in order to keep the mission running
smoothly and efficiently , we have to
try to negate those hazards before they
become an issue . Serving as a safety
specialist here in Altadena is near and
dear to my heart because I have family
in the area , so making sure that the
crews complete the mission safely is my
way of giving back to the community .
